explanation: Amphibians live on both land and water, sharing several unifying characteristics: 1) Limbs: normally tetrapods (having 4 limbs); 2) Smooth, non-scaly skin: adapted for maintaining water balance; 3) Lungs: if present, they are small and used for gas exchange; 4) Double-looped circulatory pathway, featuring a 3-chambered heart; 5) terrestrial-adapted sense organs (sight, hearing, smell); and 6) Ectothermy (body temperature dependent on the environment). Amphibians rely on aquatic reproduction, depositing jelly-coated eggs in water where they are fertilized. The young hatch and grow in water before emerging as terrestrial adults. Amphibian diversity includes salamanders and newts, frogs and toads, and caecilians.

opts: Open circulatory system with no specialized heart
